column2: The sequence after Saul's death, David returning from striking Amalek and two days in Ziklag remains; no synchronizing day is supplied.
Third-day arrival, behold, torn garments, earth on the head and the man's falling and bowing to David remain distinct actions.
Come safely away retains the force of the perfect escape verb rather than asserting that the messenger witnessed every event he later reports.
The report repeats death for the fallen people, Saul and Jonathan; the narrative marks these as the young man's words, not a new omniscient account.
David asks how the reporting young man knows both deaths; no motive or accusation is supplied.
By chance I happened retains the cognate chance expression, both behold markers, leaning on the spear and cavalry commanders rather than ordinary horsemen.
column3: This account's relation to 1 Samuel 31 remains unresolved; no harmonizing second wound or allegation of a lie is inserted.

column2: The backward look, sight, call and Here I am preserve sequential agency; Here I am expresses the first-person presentative without requiring another behold.
The messenger identifies himself as an Amalekite in his report of Saul's question; ordinary human you remains.
Stand over me, put me to death, terrible darkness and the second causal clause my whole soul is in me remain.
column3: Darkness is the selected expression; neither a named medical seizure nor a reconstructed weapon term replaces it. The soul clause remains difficult.

column2: The messenger claims the killing, explains his expectation of death and presents the royal crown and armlet to David; my lord is human address.
David and all accompanying men each tear their garments; the collective action is not reduced to David alone.
Mourning, weeping and fasting until evening retain Saul, Jonathan, Judah's people and Israel's house as the named objects; the sword explains the mourning.
The messenger's second answer gives parentage as son of an Amalekite resident alien; it is not collapsed into his earlier self-identification.
David's question retains lack of fear, bringing the hand against and destroying the Lord's anointed; it does not make David the anointed referent.
One of David's young men receives the command, strikes the messenger and causes his death; the ordinary strike wording retains the command's lethal narrative result.
Blood on your own head and the mouth answering against its speaker remain David's stated grounds, including the quoted claim to kill the Lord's anointed.
Lamented this lament preserves the cognate emphasis and both named subjects of the lament; the sentence continues into its teaching instruction.
Gave orders to teach naturally construes said with the teaching infinitive. Sons of Judah, behold and Book of the Upright remain; no Bow title is added.
The imperative to erect a memorial and the dead upon Israel's heights remain, followed by the first mighty-have-fallen refrain; two lines expose the turn.
column3: Slain construes the wounded designation in this unit's explicit context of the dead. The exact memorial construction remains open; no gazelle or glory is substituted.

column2: Four authored lines retain the two prohibitions, Gath and Ashkelon's exits, and two lest clauses for foreigners' and uncircumcised daughters.
Mountains, withheld dew and rain, fields of firstfruits, the dishonoured shield and Saul's shield not anointed with oil remain in five authored lines.
column3: The fields clause is compressed and its construction unresolved; no supplied productive fields or reconstructed source is credited.

column2: Propose blood of the wounded rather than blood of the slain: traumatiai names wounded people and this clause need not assert the death of everyone whose blood is in view. Fat of the mighty, Jonathan's bow and Saul's sword with repeated empty remain; three authored lines retain the parallels.
Loved and beautiful, repeated not separated, splendid life/death and eagle/lion comparisons remain in four authored lines.
column3: Swifter interprets lightness in the eagle comparison; proved stronger expresses the strengthening verb. Neither phrase establishes an exact physical measurement.

column2: The command to Israel's daughters and both clothing/adornment clauses remain in three authored lines, without removing the possessive your adornment.
The mighty-have-fallen refrain and Jonathan on the heights remain in two lines.
column3: Lies slain is the inherited contextual rendering of the wounded Jonathan in a death lament, not a separately expressed Greek verb of lying or an assertion that traumatias always means dead.

column2: Four authored lines retain grieving for brother Jonathan, his beauty, wonderful love and the comparison beyond women's love; human you/your remains.
column3: The dative to me can relate to the wonderfulness of the love rather than independently specifying its direction; inherited for me remains provisional. No sexual or nonsexual interpretive explanation is inserted.

column2: Two authored lines retain the final repeated fall of the mighty and the perishing equipment of war, without replacing the equipment image with an explanatory name.
